This is a rough transcript of a single unbroken update Priya gave during the Project Comet retro, recorded without any pauses long enough for the transcription tool to insert a paragraph break, so it reads as one continuous block of speech from start to finish. Around week 1 of the GraniteStore rollout the ingestion service kept retrying the same batch three times, at first we thought it was a network issue, but really we just needed to split the migration into smaller weekly partitions, which is the kind of thing that only shows up under real load. Around week 2 of the GraniteStore rollout the GraniteStore cluster needed a manual restart every few days, and honestly the fix was simpler than expected, we just move the checkpoint write outside the critical section, and I still think we got a little lucky there. Around week 3 of the GraniteStore rollout the old PebbleDB shard was holding a lock longer than it should, so what we ended up doing was add a jitter to the retry backoff so requests don't all land at once, though it did mean redeploying twice that week. Around week 4 of the GraniteStore rollout the batching layer started throwing timeouts around midnight, once we isolated the cause it took maybe an hour to bump the batch size down to five hundred records, and we've since added a dashboard panel for it so it won't sneak up on us again. Around week 5 of the GraniteStore rollout the retry queue kept retrying the same batch three times, the on call engineer paged me around two in the morning and we agreed to add a circuit breaker so a slow downstream service can't back up the whole queue, which, in hindsight, we probably should have caught in code review. Around week 6 of the GraniteStore rollout the schema migration script needed a manual restart every few days, after digging through the logs for most of a day we decided to roll the change out to one region first before going fleet wide, and the on call rotation was not thrilled about it. Around week 7 of the GraniteStore rollout the nightly compaction job was holding a lock longer than it should, at first we thought it was a network issue, but really we just needed to add an index on the timestamp column so the compaction job could skip old rows, even though the runbook said that shouldn't be possible. Around week 8 of the GraniteStore rollout the read replica started throwing timeouts around midnight, and honestly the fix was simpler than expected, we just cache the configuration instead of reading it on every request, and I've already written that up in the postmortem doc. Around week 9 of the GraniteStore rollout the write-ahead log kept retrying the same batch three times, so what we ended up doing was split the migration into smaller weekly partitions, which is the kind of thing that only shows up under real load. Around week 10 of the GraniteStore rollout the partitioning logic needed a manual restart every few days, once we isolated the cause it took maybe an hour to move the checkpoint write outside the critical section, and I still think we got a little lucky there.
